blocks.title: Hashes and Merkle trees
blocks.summary: How one short fingerprint can vouch for gigabytes of data, and prove any piece of it with a handful of hashes.

blocks.title: State machine replication
blocks.summary: Run the same deterministic program on several servers, feed them the same inputs in the same order, and they stay in step.

blocks.title: Byzantine faults and agreement
blocks.summary: What happens when some machines don't just crash, but lie, and why you need more than three honest nodes for every traitor.

blocks.title: Ethereum
blocks.summary: A replicated state machine that anyone can program: accounts, the EVM, gas, tokens, and the move to proof of stake.

blocks.title: Chainlink and oracles
blocks.summary: A blockchain can't see the outside world. Oracle networks bring data in, using the same fault-tolerance ideas as the chain itself.
